title: Operational performance manifest for model onboarding and version pinning
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create and operationalize a machine-readable 'Performance Manifest' for every model/version we onboard. The manifest is a signed JSON artifact that contains latency P50/P95, throughput characteristics, cost-per-token estimate, compatible quantization profiles, and rollback/fallback mappings. This ticket scopes the product contract, consumption API, and the publishing workflow so engineering, console, and internal ops can reliably pin to verified profiles and automate rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A schema (v1) for Performance Manifest is published in Confluence and added to the schema registry
Manifest signing mechanism implemented: manifests generated at publish time include an HMAC signature and schemaVersion field
Redwood Console displays the manifest for each onboarded model under the 'Profiles' tab and exposes a 'Pin to manifest' action
Runtime can read a manifest and enforce routing to a pinned model variant with automatic fallback to preconfigured fallback variants
End-to-end tests exist: publishing flow -> manifest visible in Console -> runtime honors pin in canary environment
Backward compatibility: older schemaVersion manifests do not break agent rollout and are surfaced with deprecation warning
updates: 2025-11-14: Kickoff meeting with Eng(runtime), Console, and Security. Agreed scope: schema + signing + Console UX + runtime consumption API.
2025-12-02: Spike completed by Eng(runtime). Kernel-level profiling captured P50/P95 and cold-start graphs. Findings: KV cache warm-up dominates first 20 tokens for long-seq models.

2026-01-07: Draft manifest schema uploaded to Confluence: includes fields for latency percentiles, throughput profile, cost_estimate_usd_per_1k_tokens, quantization_compat list, hardware_affinity hints, and rollback_map.
2026-01-20: Security review workshop. Decided on HMAC signatures with key rotation; HSM integration deferred to Private deployments follow-up.

2026-02-05: Console team delivered initial UI mockups and a 'Pin manifest' modal. PM feedback requested clearer labelling for 'cost estimate' and a link to the benchmark run that generated the manifest.
2026-02-18: Eng(runtime) opened PR #4729 to add manifest consumption endpoints and a toggle to enable strict-pinning in canary clusters. Pull request connected to CI perf tests.
decisions: Use a JSON manifest (schema v1) rather than embedding profile metadata in DB fields to make manifests portable between environments
Signing with HMAC SHA256 and a versioned signing key managed in the platform vault. Public-key signatures postponed until customer ask (Private path).
Include both aggregated percentiles (P50,P95,P99) and sample token-time series metadata to help debug outliers
Cost estimate is an advisory field (not authoritative billing) and must be tied to the benchmark artifact link

Runtime will implement a 'soft' and 'strict' pinning mode: soft honors manifest preference but can fall back to compatible non-pinned variants; strict refuses non-matching variants and triggers alerting.
next_steps: Finish runtime PR feedback loop and merge manifest consumption endpoints (ENG)
Console: implement manifest view and pin modal; add link to benchmark run and cost-breakdown expanders
Prepare a validation job that automatically generates manifests from the existing verified benchmark pipeline and posts them to the manifest registry (automation)
Write canary rollout playbook and add a rollback runbook that references manifest.rollback_map
Coordinate a cross-team demo for 2026-03-01 to validate end-to-end flow and gather stakeholder sign-off
notes: Avoid coupling the manifest registry with user billing system in v1. The manifest should be purely operational metadata with an explicit link to the authoritative cost pipeline. Keep manifest schema minimal to reduce churn, and rely on schemaVersioning for future additions. Track adoption via telemetry: percent of pinned requests, number of manifests published per week, and incidents where fallback was used.
